title: Challenge 9 Quiz - Dessetra Professional Trading Methodologies
description: Test your understanding of the proprietary Dessetra Trading Methodologies, including the Moving Average Rule, Moving Average and MACD Method, Support & Resistance Zones, and Trendline Trading.

questions.question: According to the Dessetra Moving Average Rule, which EMA alignment correctly represents an uptrend?
questions.explanation: In a bullish trend, the 21 EMA should be above the 50 EMA, while the 50 EMA remains above the 200 EMA.

questions.question: When using the Dessetra Moving Average Rule, where is the preferred buy entry during an uptrend?
options: Immediately after a large bullish candle
After price retraces toward the 21 EMA or 50 EMA and provides confirmation
Whenever price moves above the 200 EMA
questions.explanation: The methodology teaches traders to wait for a retracement to the 21 EMA or 50 EMA before looking for confirmation.

questions.question: What MACD settings are used in the Dessetra Moving Average and MACD Method?
questions.explanation: The Dessetra methodology uses a MACD configuration of Fast 3, Slow 9 and Signal 16.

questions.question: Within the Dessetra methodology, what does an upward MACD Signal Line crossing through the Zero Line indicate?
options: A signal to close all trades
questions.explanation: An upward crossing through the Zero Line is treated as bullish momentum confirmation and should support—not replace—the Moving Average Rule.

questions.question: According to the Dessetra Support and Resistance Method, which market visits are generally preferred for trading?
options: The second and third visit after the zone has already shown a reaction
Any visit regardless of previous reactions
questions.explanation: The methodology often seeks opportunities from the second and third visit because the market has already demonstrated respect for the zone.

questions.question: Why does the Dessetra methodology analyse lower timeframes after identifying a support or resistance zone on a higher timeframe?
options: To reduce the number of indicators
To obtain better confirmation and more precise entries
questions.explanation: Higher timeframes identify important zones while lower timeframes provide better confirmation and more accurate entries.

questions.question: For an uptrend trendline, how should the line be drawn?
options: Connecting at least two resistance points
Connecting at least two support points (higher lows)
Across the middle of the chart
questions.explanation: An uptrend trendline is drawn by connecting at least two significant higher lows.

questions.question: Which timeframes are most suitable for the Dessetra Trendline Method?
questions.explanation: The methodology is primarily designed for the 15-minute, 1-hour and 4-hour timeframes.

questions.question: What should a trader do after price retraces back to a valid trendline?
options: Wait for market confirmation before considering an entry
Ignore the trendline and trade against it
questions.explanation: Trendlines identify potential reaction zones. Confirmation should still be obtained before entering a trade.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes the Dessetra Professional Trading Methodologies?
options: Every indicator independently guarantees profitable trades
Trend, confirmation, patience and disciplined risk management should work together before entering a trade
Only MACD is necessary for professional trading
Support and resistance should be traded without confirmation
questions.explanation: The Dessetra methodologies combine trend identification, confirmation, patience and disciplined risk management rather than relying on a single indicator.
